q: The Hardy-Littlewood maximal function Mf(x) = sup_{r>0} (1/|B(x,r)|) ∫_{B(x,r)} |f| is weak-type (1,1), meaning:
opts: μ({Mf > λ}) ≤ C||f||₁/λ for all λ > 0
exp: The maximal function is not in L¹ generally (Mf(x) ≥ c/|x|ⁿ for f = 1_{B(0,1)}), but satisfies the weak-type bound. This implies the Lebesgue differentiation theorem: (1/|B(x,r)|)∫_{B(x,r)} f → f(x) a.e.
